I would like you to implement a module named TopModule with the following
interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  x (4 bits)
 - output f

The module should implement the function f shown in the Karnaugh map
below.

             x[0]x[1]
x[2]x[3]  00  01  11  10
  00     | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
  01     | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
  11     | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
  10     | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 |

","interface":{"top":"TopModule","ports":[{"name":"x","direction":"input","width":4,"signed":false},{"name":"f","direction":"output","width":1,"signed":false}]},"constraints":"SystemVerilog, exactly one self-contained TopModule DUT. Row 10:

all zeros.

12: 1 1 0 0
14: 1 1 1 0

- 4,5: x3=0,x2=1,x1=0 → ~x3 & x2 & ~x1. But 6 has x3=0,x2=1,x1=1. So 4,5,6 form a 2-cell? Actually 4,5,6: x3=0, x2=1, and x1 varies, x0 varies. 4=0100,5=0101,6=0110. 4&5 differ in x0 only (x1=0). 4&6 differ in x1 and x0 (differs 2 bits). Hmm not adjacent. Let me redo with gray.
